explanation: Suriname covers about 164,000 km², a little under Uruguay's 181,000 km². It is also the only South American country with Dutch as its official language.

claims.text: Suriname is the smallest independent country in South America by area.
Uruguay, about 181,000 km², Guyana, about 215,000 km², and Ecuador, about 277,000 km², are each larger than Suriname.
Suriname is the only independent South American country whose official language is Dutch.

Languages: SUR nld; no other independent South American entry lists Dutch (c4). 'Independent' in the stem excludes French Guiana (part of France) and the Falkland Islands. Rival test: Uruguay is the confident wrong answer, the small country everyone pictures between giants, which makes the item counterintuitive; Guyana and Ecuador look small on maps too. Against the key: none. Volatility: evergreen, settled geography with no review date; no time words, and nothing depends on knowledge newer than mid-2026. Regional: a South American map question with no local knowledge needed. Style: Oxford spelling, plain hyphens only, straight quotes, explanation of 25 words. Myths: every claim screened against content/reference/myths.json; no match. Mystery and encore: nothing of either kind to check in a practice item. Doubts: the Uruguay margin is about 10 per cent, comfortable against any published area.

issues.note: Area figures vary by definition. Uruguay is also widely given as 176,215 km², and Ecuador as about 283,600 km² with its islands and waters (the 277,000 here is its land figure). The comparison holds either way; 'about 180,000' and 'about 280,000', or no figures, would spare a pedant's report.
